findings.issue: Wrong grammar fact: 一番 in チェスを一番どうですか is numeral 一 + counter 番 ('one game/bout', as in 一番勝負), matching the translation 'a game of chess'. It is NOT the adverbial/superlative 一番 ('first of all / the most'), which the explanation teaches.
findings.current: 一番 (いちばん) appears with the sense 'first of all/how about it for a start', the adverbial use of 一番, the same item that in comparisons means 'the most...'
findings.suggested: 一番 here is numeral 一 + counter 番, 'one game/bout' (cf. 一番勝負): チェスを一番どうですか = 'how about a game of chess?'

findings.issue: Same wrong grammar fact as expl_en: 一番 here is numeral 一 + contador 番 ('uma partida/um round', como em 一番勝負), not the adverbial/superlative 一番 ('antes de mais nada / o mais'). The explanation teaches a false identification of the morpheme.
findings.current: 一番 (いちばん) aparece aqui com o sentido de 'antes de mais nada / que tal de uma vez', é o uso adverbial de 一番 (o alvo)
findings.suggested: 一番 aqui é o numeral 一 + contador 番: 'uma partida/um round' (cf. 一番勝負); チェスを一番どうですか = 'que tal uma partida de xadrez?'

findings.issue: Sense-changing mistranslation: 家を出る means 'leave home / move out', not 'sell my house'. The en contradicts the jp and the record's own pt ('sair de casa') and lit_en ('leaving home').
findings.current: Even if I have to sell my house, I'll keep my business going.
findings.suggested: Even if it comes to leaving my home, I'll keep my business going.

findings.issue: Corrupt token list: stray tokens 出 (で) and かける sit at positions 0-1, before ちょうど, with all-null glosses, duplicating the properly glossed 出かける token at position 3. Order no longer matches the sentence; the dissection would display 出かける twice.
findings.current: {"s":"出","r":"で"} and {"s":"かける","r":"かける"} inserted before ちょうど
findings.suggested: Delete the two stray null tokens; list should be ちょうど・出かける・ところ・だ・。

findings.issue: Gloss gives the wrong sense in context: 一番 here means 'one game/round' (counter 番 for bouts), not 'right away / first of all'. Conflicts with the correct en translation 'a game of chess'.
findings.current: how about right away / first of all (lit. number one)
findings.suggested: one game, a round (numeral 一 + counter 番 for bouts/matches)

findings.issue: Inaccurate literal mirror: を rendered as 'At' instead of object marker, 一番 as 'number one' instead of 'one game', and '(he)' is invented — どうですか has no third-person subject.
findings.current: At chess, number one, how is (he)?
findings.suggested: Chess (object), one game — how is it (= how about it)?

findings.issue: Literal mirror uses the wrong sense of 一番: 'número-um' instead of 'uma partida' (numeral + contador 番).
findings.suggested: Xadrez (objeto), uma partida — como é (= que tal)?

findings.issue: JP is a plain statement of reason + action; the en recasts it as a permission request ('I'd like..., please') and turns ちょっと ('a little hot') into 'too hot'. The record's pt and lit_en render it correctly, so en is the outlier.
findings.current: I'd like to take my jacket off, please; it's too hot.
findings.suggested: It's a little hot, so I'll take off my jacket.

findings.issue: Untranslated Japanese metalanguage in the pt-BR learner text: 副詞 is used where the en version says 'The adverb'. A beginner cannot read 副詞.
findings.current: 副詞 ちょっと ('um pouco') suaviza a intensidade do calor.
findings.suggested: O advérbio ちょっと ('um pouco') suaviza a intensidade do calor.

findings.issue: The operative gloss 'uma partida/uma rodada' is right, but the parenthetical claims the literal meaning is 'número um', which is the other sense of 一番; literally it is 一 + contador 番 ('uma partida'). Inconsistent with the needed expl fix.
findings.current: que tal uma partida/uma rodada (lit. 'número um', aqui no sentido de jogar uma vez)
findings.suggested: uma partida, uma rodada (numeral 一 + contador 番 de partidas)

findings.issue: Wrong romanization of ちぇ: 'chiesu' would read ちえす; ちぇ is 'che'. (Not the known punctuation/katakana-passthrough issue — the kana was converted but incorrectly.)

Awkward pt-BR needing a parenthetical crutch: 'Estou bem na hora de sair (já vou)' is not an idiomatic rendering of 'I'm just about to leave', and natural-translation fields should not carry parenthetical glosses.
findings.current: Estou bem na hora de sair (já vou).
